three_things_countdown.description: Have the narrator promise exactly three things a tool does better than people expect. Show each as a big numbered caption on a 3D panel, with a before/after file or size change.
three_things_countdown.hook_pattern: [Famous product] is here, and it has N things [rivals] need to copy

survives_the_torture_test.description: Show a 3D character throwing everything at a file or form (wrong size, locked, corrupted, too big), and the tool still works. The narrator names each trial while the panel shows the error turning into success.
survives_the_torture_test.hook_pattern: This [thing] can survive anything, so even if you do this, this, or this, nothing happens

one_thing_replaces_many.description: Show a character juggling several separate apps or sites for a job, and the narrator reveals a single site that does it all, with the extra apps vanishing from the 3D scene.

two_in_one_claim.description: Open with the first word at 0 s, state that the tool does two jobs people think need two apps, and show both outcomes side by side in two 3D panels.
two_in_one_claim.hook_pattern: This [device] can work like a [A] and a [B]

before_after_gap.description: Show the same file handled the old painful way and then with our tool, in two matching panels. The narrator names the gap in one line and keeps it short.

one_gesture_fix.description: Open on a character stuck in a small, painful form problem, then have them fix it with one single action in the tool. End on the proof panel (size or success) and one useful number.
one_gesture_fix.hook_pattern: The most useful [thing] you can actually buy for [moment of annoyance]

scary_checklist_countdown.description: Narrate a short story where a character is told something quietly alarming about their files. They run N quick checks one by one, each shown on a panel, and the last check gives the biggest surprise before the fix.
scary_checklist_countdown.hook_pattern: Your [personal thing] may already be [exposed/lost]. Open these N sites/tools, and the last one is the scariest.

claim_then_three_proofs.description: Have the narrator make one big claim about a tool, then let a character prove it with three quick, concrete results shown on panels, ending with a short verdict.
claim_then_three_proofs.hook_pattern: This is the most [superlative] [thing] ever. It has 3 features, and here is proof of each.

everyday_analogy_explainer.description: Narrate a tiny story where a character's file problem is explained with one everyday comparison (such as a water tank or a suitcase). Then escalate with 'what if it had been worse?' before the fix.
everyday_analogy_explainer.hook_pattern: Even [a giant] was [hit/caught out] in one day, and nobody noticed. Here is how it happened and what you should do.

relatable_roast_reassure.description: Have a recurring character tease a classmate for a small file panic, then reassure them that everyone has been stuck there and show the one-tap fix.
relatable_roast_reassure.hook_pattern: Oh, you look like you don't know [what students always worry about]. Everybody was once confused.
